breakdown.description: The prompt imposes zero transverse strain on a freely loaded uniaxial rod, which contradicts the Poisson-effect calculation the problem asks for.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly retains the plane strain assumption (ε_x = ε_y = 0) from the incomplete prompt, setting up the constraint equations accordingly. The ground truth removes this constraint entirely, treating the rod as a standard uniaxial member free to deform laterally via the Poisson effect. The agent repeated the original error instead of correcting it.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats Poisson’s ratio as irrelevant even though the requested diameter change depends directly on the lateral strain relation.
breakdown.reason: Because the plane strain assumption is preserved, the generated spec concludes that the lateral strain is zero and therefore Δd = 0. This renders Poisson's ratio irrelevant to the diameter change calculation, which is exactly the inconsistency identified. The ground truth requires ε_lat = –ν × ε_z (standard Poisson relation) so that ν = 0.29 is directly used to compute the change in diameter.
